newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries open steady ahead of ECI report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries open steady ahead of ECI report.

text.p: U.S. Treasury securities prices were steady at Tuesday's opening as the market awaited the second quarter Employment Cost Index (ECI), set for release at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.

Helping to support the bond market was news of a balanced budget pact between Republicans and Democrats in Washington. However, traders said that such an agreement had largely been priced into the market already.
Economists polled by Reuters expected, on average, that the second quarter ECI would rise by 0.8 percent, as opposed to the 0.6 percent increase in the first quarter.
"We expect to see a rise of 0.7 percent on the ECI, and if we're correct that allows the market to charge to new highs," said Patrick Dimick, trader at UBS Securities.
However, Dimick expressed worry that the market could feed on itself as more investors swapped out of mortgage-backed securities and into Treasuries.
"This thing could begin to snowball, and that's the main risk on the upside," Dimick said. "The risk to the upside is if the benefits side rises (more than expected).
Increases in benefits costs have offset wage rises in recent quarters.
Dimick said a rise of anything more than 0.3 percent would be cause for concern to Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
The ECI had been a relatively obscure figure until Greenspan told Congress he eyed it as an indicator of future inflation. Benefit costs rose 0.6 percent in the second quarter.
However, other analysts argued that benefit costs remained contained and the jump seen in the second quarter was merely due to problems the Bureau of Labor Stastistics had in measuring the figure.
The Treasury's 30-year bond was trading down 3/32 at 102-26 to yield 6.41 percent.

The two-year note was up 1/32 at 100-3/32 to yield 5.83 percent. The five-year note was unchanged at 99-28/32 to yield 6.03 percent, while the 10-year note also was unchanged at 103-19/32 to yield 6.13 percent.
Three-month bills were unchanged at 5.11 percent and six-month bills were down one basis point at 5.13 percent. Year bills were one basis point lower at 5.20 percent.
(( -- John P. Hughes, N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1663 ))
